questions.stem: A nonrebreathing system with a reservoir bag and a one-way valve that vents every exhaled breath is classified as:
questions.explanation: Reservoir-equipped systems that exhaust exhaled gas without rebreathing are semi-open. The reservoir distinguishes them from open systems.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 101 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Assuming no leaks, a circle system supplies fresh gas at the patient's oxygen uptake rate, absorbs CO₂, and retains the remaining exhaled gas. How is it classified?
questions.explanation: A closed circle system adds only enough fresh gas to replace patient uptake while carbon dioxide is chemically absorbed. This permits rebreathing of the remaining exhaled gas.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 101 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Open-drop delivery of agent onto a mask with no bag or valves is classified as:
questions.explanation: Open-drop anesthesia lacks a reservoir bag and does not return exhaled gas to the patient. It is an open breathing system.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 101 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Which two features define the traditional classification of breathing circuits?
options: Reservoir present and degree of rebreathing
Absorber present and fresh gas flow rate
Ventilation mode and the agent used
Number of valves and length of tubing
questions.explanation: The traditional classification is based on whether a reservoir is present and the degree of rebreathing. Hardware configuration and fresh-gas flow further describe circuit function.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 101 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: In a circle system, which exhaled gas is removed before rebreathing?
questions.explanation: The carbon dioxide absorber removes exhaled CO₂ before gas returns to the inspiratory limb. Oxygen and anesthetic gases may also be retained or replenished.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 101 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: For an adult with minute ventilation of 6 L/min, what fresh-gas-flow range corresponds to the textbook's approximate 1–1.5 times minute-ventilation rule for dilution-only CO₂ removal?
questions.explanation: The chapter's approximate dilution-only requirement is 1–1.5 times minute ventilation, yielding 6–9 L/min here. Actual requirements depend on circuit configuration and breathing pattern.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 101 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Why does CO2 removal by dilution depend on inflow site and valve location as well as FGF?
options: CO2 is exhaled only intermittently while fresh gas flows continuously
Fresh gas reacts with CO2 at the inflow site
CO2 is exhaled continuously while fresh gas flows intermittently
questions.explanation: Fresh gas enters continuously, but exhaled CO₂ arrives primarily during expiration. Inlet and valve positions determine how efficiently fresh gas clears expired gas.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 101 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Which component of a breathing circuit leads excess gas to the scavenger?
questions.explanation: The adjustable pressure-limiting valve vents excess circuit gas to the scavenging system during manual or spontaneous ventilation. Its setting also affects circuit pressure.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 106 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Monitoring tidal volume, respiratory rate, airway pressure, and gas concentrations serves which function of a breathing circuit?
questions.explanation: A breathing circuit supports monitoring of airway pressure, tidal volume, respiratory rate, and inspired or expired gas concentrations through connected sensors.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 101 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Using the textbook estimate of 400–500 mL/m, what is the internal volume of 3 m of standard breathing tubing?
questions.explanation: At a nominal 400–500 mL per meter, three meters of tubing contains about 1.2–1.5 L. Actual internal volume varies with tubing diameter and design.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 102 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Concertina tubing is stretched from 50 cm to 2 m. What happens to circuit resistance?
questions.explanation: The textbook states that concertina extensions can stretch from about 50 cm to 2 m without appreciably increasing flow resistance. Their compliant volume may still affect measured ventilation.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 103 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Why are breathing tubes corrugated or spiral-reinforced?
questions.explanation: Corrugations let breathing tubing bend without readily kinking, helping maintain gas flow as the circuit is repositioned.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 102 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Corrugations in breathing tubing promote which types of gas mixing?
questions.explanation: The corrugations promote turbulent flow and both radial and longitudinal mixing. The amount of mixing depends on flow conditions and tube geometry.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 103 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Large-bore (22 mm) breathing tubing is chosen mainly to:
questions.explanation: Using wider breathing tubing decreases resistance to gas movement and helps limit the work or pressure needed for ventilation.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 102 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: During a breathing-system pressure leak test, circuit pressure cannot be maintained despite appropriate adjustable pressure-limiting valve closure and continuous oxygen inflow. What should be suspected?
options: An adjustable pressure-limiting valve that is excessively tight
An obstruction proven by this pressure test alone
A significant leak in the breathing system
questions.explanation: Failure to maintain circuit pressure during a properly performed leak test raises concern for a breathing-system leak. Pressure leak testing alone does not exclude obstruction or confirm correct unidirectional-valve operation; those require separate flow and functional checks.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 25, printed pp. 572–573

questions.stem: When does the expiratory unidirectional valve open?
options: Only when the APL is open
questions.explanation: The expiratory one-way valve opens when exhaled gas flows from the patient toward the expiratory limb and closes against reverse inspiratory flow.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 103 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Unidirectional valves in breathing circuits need which two essential characteristics?
questions.explanation: Unidirectional valves should open with minimal pressure and seal effectively in the reverse direction. Sticking or leakage can increase resistance or permit rebreathing.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 103 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Both unidirectional valves are working, but the patient's mask is replaced with a long extension and HME between the Y and the face. What happens to apparatus dead space?
options: It increases by the volume of the added parts
It is unchanged because the valves are competent
It becomes the whole expiratory limb
It decreases because flow becomes laminar
questions.explanation: Apparatus placed between the Y-piece and the patient adds volume in which exhaled gas may remain between breaths. An extension or heat-moisture exchanger therefore can increase apparatus dead space.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 104 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: The inspiratory valve is stuck open. During exhalation, where can exhaled gas go?
options: Back into the inspiratory limb to be rebreathed
Only through the expiratory limb to the absorber
Nowhere, because the circuit becomes occluded
Directly to the scavenger through the APL only
questions.explanation: An incompetent inspiratory valve can permit exhaled gas to enter the inspiratory limb. That gas may return to the patient on the next inspiration, increasing rebreathing.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 103–104 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Which material property keeps a valve disk from sticking from condensation?
questions.explanation: Hydrophobic valve materials reduce water adhesion and may help prevent condensation from making the valve disk stick.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 104 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Condensation makes a valve disk stick to its knife edge. What is the most immediate effect?
questions.explanation: A wet or adhering valve disk may require extra pressure to open. This raises circuit resistance and can impair spontaneous breathing.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 104 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Which finding most strongly suggests a malfunctioning unidirectional valve rather than exhausted CO₂ absorbent?
options: Rebreathing that persists after new absorbent
Falling EtCO2 at high fresh gas flow
Low airway pressure from a circuit leak
questions.explanation: Persistent inspired CO₂ after absorbent replacement points toward valve incompetence or another circuit fault rather than absorbent exhaustion alone. The textbook explains that a valve failing to seal permits rebreathing, whereas a functional absorbent chemically removes CO₂.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp 104, 107 (complete revised answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: During low-flow spontaneous mask ventilation, reservoir-bag excursions suddenly cease after previously being visible. What concern requires immediate assessment?
options: A correct APL setting for spontaneous breaths
Excessive fresh gas flow filling the bag
Normal deep anesthesia with slow breaths
Possible loss of ventilation; immediately assess the patient and airway
questions.explanation: At low fresh-gas flow, reservoir-bag motion generally reflects patient ventilation. Sudden loss of motion warrants immediate assessment of breathing, the airway, and the circuit; the bag alone is not a definitive monitor.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 105 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Reservoir bags come in what size range?
questions.explanation: The textbook describes reservoir bags ranging from 0.5 to 6 L. The selected bag should exceed the patient's inspiratory capacity so a deep breath does not empty it.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 105 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: A 1-L bag is used on a large adult breathing spontaneously. What is likely?
options: A deep breath empties the bag
The bag overdistends and raises pressure
questions.explanation: A reservoir bag that is too small may empty during a large spontaneous inspiration, increasing resistance to adequate gas delivery.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 105 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: In a circle system, the reservoir bag usually connects where?
options: Near the absorber via a T-fitting by the pop-off
In the inspiratory limb after the valve
At the common gas outlet on the machine
At the Y-piece next to the patient connection
questions.explanation: In many circle systems the reservoir bag attaches near the absorber and adjustable pressure-limiting valve. Exact connections vary among workstations.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 105–106 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: In the traditional common-gas-outlet arrangement described in the textbook, how does fresh gas reach the breathing circuit?
options: Thick-walled tubing from the common gas outlet
The expiratory limb of the circle system
questions.explanation: The traditional common gas outlet connects to the breathing circuit through thick-walled tubing. Some newer workstations use integrated fresh-gas delivery paths instead.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 106 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Why is fresh gas inflow placed between the absorber and the inspiratory valve rather than in the expiratory limb?
options: It lowers inspired O2 to reduce fire risk
It speeds absorber exhaustion for faster changes
It warms fresh gas by passing it through the absorber
Fresh gas reaches the patient before being vented
questions.explanation: Introducing fresh gas near the inspiratory side reduces premature loss of fresh gas through the expiratory outlet and helps deliver it to the patient.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 113 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: At steady state, the APL valve vents excess circuit gas in relation to which incoming flow?
questions.explanation: The APL valve releases excess gas associated with fresh-gas inflow, after accounting for patient uptake and leaks. Its pressure setting controls when gas can leave the circuit.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 106 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: When a spring-loaded APL valve is partially tightened during manual ventilation, what does this permit?
questions.explanation: Partially tightening a spring-loaded APL valve raises the pressure required for gas to escape. Proper adjustment permits pressure-limited manual ventilation.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 106 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: What characterizes the reservoir in a Mapleson circuit?
options: It is packed with CO2 absorbent granules
Only fresh gas can ever fill it
Fresh gas, exhaled gas, or both can fill it
Only exhaled gas can ever fill it
questions.explanation: A Mapleson reservoir may contain fresh gas, exhaled gas, or a mixture depending on the circuit layout and phase of breathing.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 114 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: CO2 elimination in a Mapleson circuit is critically affected by which two factors?
options: Total FGF and the breathing pattern
Absorber size and unidirectional valve type
questions.explanation: Mapleson circuits lack chemical CO₂ absorption, making fresh-gas flow and spontaneous versus controlled breathing important determinants of rebreathing.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 114 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: During spontaneous breathing in a Mapleson circuit, at what point is CO₂-rich exhaled gas preferentially vented through an appropriately located pop-off valve?
questions.explanation: The textbook identifies end-exhalation as the time when CO₂-rich gas can be vented at pressure above atmospheric during spontaneous breathing. Pop-off location affects how efficiently the circuit eliminates CO₂.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 114–115 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: The Lack circuit is a variant of which Mapleson type?
questions.explanation: The Lack system is a coaxial modification of the Mapleson A arrangement, intended to preserve its spontaneous-breathing characteristics.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 101, 117 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: When appropriately configured, which ventilation modes can the Humphrey ADE system support efficiently?
options: Neither mode without a CO2 absorber
questions.explanation: The Humphrey ADE circuit can be configured to operate in its A mode for spontaneous breathing or D/E mode for controlled ventilation.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 101, 115–117 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: What problem is expected when a Mapleson A circuit is used for controlled ventilation with insufficient fresh-gas flow?
options: Loss of agent to the absorber
questions.explanation: Mapleson A is efficient with spontaneous breathing but inefficient in controlled ventilation unless fresh-gas flow is high enough to limit CO₂ rebreathing.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 117 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Why do Mapleson circuits not need an absorber?
options: CO2 leaves through a separate limb
Fresh gas dilutes CO2 and the pop-off vents it
Their corrugated tubing chemically absorbs CO2
questions.explanation: Without an absorber, Mapleson circuits remove expired CO₂ by directing it out of the circuit and replacing it with fresh gas.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 114 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Which numbered circuit has fresh gas entering near the patient with the pop-off also at the patient end?
questions.explanation: In the conventional Mapleson B arrangement, fresh gas enters close to the patient and the expiratory valve is nearby. Confirm that numbered circuit 2 matches the attached figure.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment, 3rd ed., Ch. 4: Breathing Circuits (chapter-aligned; exact passage pending verification)

questions.stem: Which numbered circuits are most efficient for controlled ventilation?
questions.explanation: Mapleson D, E, and F are relatively efficient for controlled ventilation when appropriately configured and supplied with fresh gas. Confirm the numbered diagrams 4–6.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment, 3rd ed., Ch. 4: Breathing Circuits (chapter-aligned; exact passage pending verification)

questions.stem: A spontaneously breathing child is placed on numbered circuit 5. What part of the circuit acts as the reservoir?
options: A reservoir bag at the end
questions.explanation: A Mapleson E/T-piece has no reservoir bag. Its expiratory limb provides gas volume and a pathway for venting, but flow must be adequate to avoid rebreathing.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment, 3rd ed., Ch. 4: Breathing Circuits (chapter-aligned; exact passage pending verification)

questions.stem: Which numbered circuit has a pop-off valve located next to the reservoir bag, away from the patient?
questions.explanation: In Mapleson D, fresh gas enters near the patient while the reservoir bag and expiratory relief valve are farther away. Confirm which numbered diagram shows that layout.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment, 3rd ed., Ch. 4: Breathing Circuits (chapter-aligned; exact passage pending verification)

questions.stem: Which numbered circuit has no pop-off valve and uses an open-tailed bag?
questions.explanation: The Jackson-Rees modification of Mapleson E (Mapleson F) uses an open-tailed reservoir bag for controlled ventilation. Match the figure label before accepting circuit 6.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment, 3rd ed., Ch. 4: Breathing Circuits (chapter-aligned; exact passage pending verification)

questions.stem: Under normal conditions, why does the upper airway add heat and moisture to inspired gas?
options: To lower airway resistance in the bronchi
To raise CO2 elimination from the alveoli
To increase dead space in the trachea
To prevent drying and injury in lower airways
questions.explanation: The upper airway warms and humidifies inspired gas to protect lower-airway secretions and mucosa. Bypassing this function with an endotracheal tube increases the need for humidification.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed pp. 183 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Which device passively retains heat and moisture during anesthesia?
questions.explanation: A heat-and-moisture exchanger traps heat and moisture during expiration and returns a portion during inspiration. It works passively.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed pp. 183, 187 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: In the functional description used in Ehrenwerth's humidification chapter, where does the upper airway extend?
options: From the larynx to the alveoli
From the external nares to the major bronchi
From the lips to the larynx
From the nasopharynx to the carina only
questions.explanation: The chapter defines the functional upper airway from the external nares to the major bronchi. Other anatomical conventions may use a narrower definition.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed pp. 184 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Besides conditioning inspired gas, the upper airway has which expiratory functions?
options: Adding CO2 to and removing O2 from exhaled gas
Removing volatile agent from exhaled gas
Conserving heat and humidity; clearing particles
questions.explanation: On expiration, airway mucosa helps conserve heat and moisture, while mucociliary transport removes trapped particles.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed pp. 184 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: What creates maximal contact between inspired gas and mucosa in the nose?
options: Mucus film on the nasal hairs
questions.explanation: Nasal turbinates create airflow mixing and a large mucosal contact surface, improving warming, humidification, and filtration.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed pp. 184 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Which change is specifically described as moving the isothermic saturation boundary farther down the respiratory tract?
options: Bypassing the upper airway with an endotracheal tube
Delivering warm, fully saturated inspired gas
Using a smaller tidal volume of warm gas
questions.explanation: Endotracheal intubation bypasses much of the upper airway's normal heat-and-moisture exchange. The isothermic saturation boundary consequently shifts distally.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed pp. 184 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Which epithelium type explains why the larynx adds little humidity?
questions.explanation: Respiratory epithelium transitions in the larynx; squamous-lined regions have less capacity for active humidification. The broad claim about the entire larynx requires anatomical qualification.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment, 3rd ed., Ch. 7: Humidification and Filtration (chapter-aligned; exact passage pending verification)

questions.stem: How do mucus droplets form the film over the cilia?
options: They absorb water, swell, and coalesce
They dissolve into the inspired gas
They dry out and harden into plugs
questions.explanation: Airway secretions absorb water and form a mucus layer over epithelial cilia. This layer traps particles for mucociliary clearance.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed pp. 185 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Mucus glands keep upper airway mucosa moist by which two processes?
questions.explanation: Airway glands and mucosal surfaces contribute water through secretion and transudation, keeping the airway surface hydrated for mucociliary transport.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed pp. 185 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: After prolonged delivery of inadequately humidified gas through an endotracheal tube, which sequence is most likely?
options: Water intoxication, surfactant loss, then edema
Better compliance, then lower peak pressures
Thick mucus, slowed cilia, retention, atelectasis
Thin mucus, faster cilia, then bronchospasm
questions.explanation: Dry inspired gas thickens mucus and impairs ciliary clearance. Retained secretions can obstruct airways and contribute to atelectasis.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed pp. 185 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Underhumidification can eventually cause which mucosal changes?
questions.explanation: Prolonged exposure to inadequately humidified gas damages cilia and airway epithelium and can progress to inflammation, ulceration, or tissue injury.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed pp. 185 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Which effect of underhumidification affects lung mechanics?
questions.explanation: Mucus retention and small-airway obstruction can cause atelectasis, reducing ventilated lung volume and respiratory-system compliance.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed pp. 185 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: If inspired gas is overheated and fully saturated, what may happen as it cools within the airway?
options: A distal shift of the ISB
questions.explanation: Overheated, saturated gas may cool and condense water in the airway. Excess moisture can disrupt normal mucociliary transport and impair airway function.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed pp. 185–186 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Exhaled tidal volume readings become erratic with a heated humidifier running. What is a likely cause?
options: Low circuit compliance in the tubing
Condensed water obstructing the flow sensors
Dry gas damaging the sensors’ membranes
questions.explanation: Liquid water accumulating in a circuit or flow sensor can interfere with flow measurements and cause inaccurate or erratic displayed tidal volumes.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed pp. 186 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: According to the textbook's discussion of overhumidification, what happens to airway mucus viscosity?
questions.explanation: The chapter describes condensation of excess water as reducing mucosal viscosity. Excess humidity may nevertheless impair mucociliary transport and increase airway resistance.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed pp. 185 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Which components make up the basic structure of a heat-and-moisture exchanger (HME)?
options: A casing, inlet, outlet, and partial barrier
A one-way valve and a reservoir bag
A CO2 absorber and a one-way valve
A heated plate sitting above a water chamber
questions.explanation: A heat-and-moisture exchanger contains a housing and exchange medium that conserves heat and moisture from exhaled gas for the next inspiration.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed pp. 187 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Why is a large-volume heat-and-moisture exchanger concerning in a small infant?
options: Dead space that is large relative to Vt
questions.explanation: An HME adds internal apparatus dead space. In an infant with a small tidal volume, that extra dead space may substantially reduce effective alveolar ventilation.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed pp. 187–188 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: What does filtration efficiency measure in a specified aerosol-challenge test?
options: Dead space added by the filter
Pressure drop across the filter material
Share of test particles stopped by the filter
questions.explanation: Filtration efficiency is the percentage of challenge particles captured or prevented from passing through the filter under specified test conditions.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed pp. 186 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: If 3 of 10,000 challenge particles pass through a filter, what is its filtration efficiency?
questions.explanation: Three particles passing from 10,000 gives 0.03% penetration. Filtration efficiency is 100% − 0.03% = 99.97%.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed pp. 186 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: What do BFE and VFE stand for?
options: Barrier and vapor filtration exchange rates
questions.explanation: BFE and VFE mean bacterial filtration efficiency and viral filtration efficiency. Values depend on standardized testing conditions.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed pp. 186 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: What is an aerosol?
options: Solid or liquid particles suspended in gas
Pure water vapor with no particles at all
questions.explanation: An aerosol is a suspension of liquid droplets or solid particles in a gas; it is distinct from a true gas or vapor.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed pp. 186 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Why is high fresh-gas flow usually used before transitioning to closed-circuit anesthesia?
options: To prevent humidification of the circuit
To establish depth quickly before reducing flow
To lower vaporizer output during induction
To exhaust the absorbent before lowering flow
questions.explanation: High fresh-gas flow helps establish the intended inspired and end-tidal anesthetic tensions before flow is reduced. Once near-steady conditions are achieved, flow can be titrated toward patient uptake while concentrations are monitored.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 19, printed p. 433 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: During a high-flow induction followed by closed-circuit maintenance, when is fresh-gas flow usually reduced?
options: After inspired and end-tidal gas tensions approach their intended targets
questions.explanation: Fresh-gas flow is commonly reduced after the desired anesthetic state approaches steady conditions. Inspired oxygen and anesthetic concentrations still require monitoring and adjustment as patient uptake changes.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 19, printed p. 433 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: In a leak-free, truly closed circuit with stable gas composition, how can patient oxygen consumption be estimated?
options: From the vaporizer dial setting over time
From the oxygen flow needed to maintain circuit volume and oxygen concentration
From the size of the reservoir bag
questions.explanation: In a truly closed circuit at steady state, oxygen delivery balances the patient's oxygen uptake. The oxygen flow needed to maintain stable circuit volume and composition therefore estimates oxygen consumption.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 19, printed p. 441 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: After carbon dioxide absorption, why is exhaled gas useful for rebreathing in a closed circuit?
options: They have higher anesthetic tension than inspired gas
They are already warmed and humidified by the patient
questions.explanation: Exhaled gas has already been warmed and humidified by the patient. Once carbon dioxide is removed by the absorbent, rebreathing conserves this heat and moisture.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 19, printed p. 433 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: In a leak-free, truly closed circuit, total volume and each administered gas concentration remain constant at steady state. What must be true?
options: Fresh gas flow exceeds total uptake
The APL valve is fully open
Input of each administered gas or vapor matches its uptake
questions.explanation: At steady state, a closed circuit maintains both total volume and individual gas tensions by replacing each administered gas or vapor at its uptake rate. Constant total volume alone would not prove that every individual gas concentration is stable.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 19, printed pp. 440–441 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: In a leak-free closed circle system, the reservoir bag gradually shrinks as the patient consumes oxygen. Which adjustment corrects the gas-volume deficit?
options: Increase O2 inflow to match uptake
Open the APL to release pressure
Turn off the vaporizer to save agent
Decrease O2 inflow to match uptake
questions.explanation: In a truly closed circuit, fresh oxygen delivery must replace the patient's oxygen uptake to maintain gas volume. A shrinking reservoir bag warrants checking for leaks and, if none is present, increasing oxygen inflow to match consumption.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 19, printed p. 441 (complete revised answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: In a leak-free, closed circuit with the adjustable pressure-limiting valve closed, the reservoir bag steadily enlarges. What does this indicate?
options: Total gas inflow exceeds patient uptake
questions.explanation: With no circuit venting or leak, a growing reservoir indicates net gas accumulation. Reduce excessive inflow while monitoring circuit pressure and inspired gas concentrations.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 19, printed pp. 440–441 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: In a semiclosed low-flow breathing circuit, why can inspired oxygen fall even when oxygen inflow exceeds estimated patient uptake?
options: The vaporizer displaces oxygen from the gas
Gas vented from the breathing circuit also carries oxygen away
The machine automatically adds nitrogen at low flow
Oxygen reacts with the carbon dioxide absorbent
questions.explanation: In a semiclosed circuit, excess gas is exhausted rather than retained, and the exhausted gas contains oxygen. Oxygen delivery must account for both patient uptake and oxygen lost through circuit venting.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 19, printed pp. 448–449 (complete revised question and answer set independently verified)

questions.stem: In a truly closed circuit at steady state, with oxygen inflow balanced against consumption, what happens to inspired oxygen concentration?
questions.explanation: A stable inspired oxygen fraction requires oxygen inflow to match uptake in a closed circuit. When gas balance is maintained at steady state, the oxygen concentration remains constant.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 19, printed pp. 440–441 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: In a low-flow anesthesia example, why might fresh-gas flow be reduced after initial wash-in instead of immediately lowering the vaporizer setting?
options: Lowering the vaporizer first prevents awareness
The vaporizer can’t be adjusted at high flow
Tensions are already up; lower flow cuts waste
FGF must drop before the absorber activates
questions.explanation: Lowering fresh-gas flow reduces waste after circuit concentrations approach target values. The exact two-minute sequence is protocol-specific rather than a universal rule.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Chapter 19 (Closed-Circuit Anesthesia); specific passage/page verification pending

questions.stem: When the same end-tidal anesthetic tension is maintained, how does anesthetic depth compare between low-flow and high-flow techniques?
options: Deeper, because more agent is rebreathed
Lighter, because less agent is delivered
Comparable, because end-tidal anesthetic tension is matched
questions.explanation: Low- and high-flow techniques can maintain the same end-tidal and alveolar anesthetic tensions by using different fresh-gas and vaporizer settings. Comparable effect-site tensions, rather than flow rate itself, determine comparable anesthetic depth.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 19, printed p. 440 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: During ongoing anesthetic uptake in a semiclosed circuit, fresh-gas flow falls from 6 to 1 L/min without a vaporizer adjustment. What is the expected initial effect on inspired agent concentration?
options: It is unchanged because the dial is unchanged
It rises because less agent is vented
It falls as low-tension exhaled gas is rebreathed
It doubles because flow is lower
questions.explanation: Reducing fresh-gas flow increases the proportion of rebreathed gas, which generally contains less anesthetic than fresh gas during ongoing uptake. Inspired concentration can therefore fall unless the delivered agent concentration is adjusted.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 19, printed p. 436 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: In a semiclosed circle system, which factors determine inspired volatile anesthetic concentration?
options: Fresh-gas flow, vaporizer setting, and exhaled gas flow and anesthetic tension
The fresh gas flow rate only
The vaporizer dial setting alone, nothing else
questions.explanation: Inspired agent tension is determined by mixing the fresh-gas stream with rebreathed expired gas. Fresh-gas flow, vaporizer output, exhaled flow, and exhaled agent tension all contribute.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 19, printed pp. 436, 442 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: After reducing the vaporizer setting, why does inspired anesthetic concentration generally decrease faster with high fresh-gas flow?
options: The absorber holds agent at high fresh gas flow
Higher fresh-gas flow clears anesthetic from the circuit more quickly
Rebreathing increases at high fresh gas flow
The vaporizer overdelivers at high flows
questions.explanation: Higher fresh-gas flow speeds washout of volatile anesthetic from the breathing system after the vaporizer setting is reduced. Gas analysis remains important because elimination from patient tissues may continue.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 8, printed p. 213 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Which combination of changes can help increase alveolar sevoflurane concentration more rapidly under appropriate ventilation conditions?
options: Lower FGF and raise the dial, nothing else
Raise MV, dialed concentration, and FGF
Raise FGF and lower the dial
questions.explanation: Increasing fresh-gas flow and vaporizer output can increase inspired anesthetic concentration. Minute ventilation may influence alveolar equilibration, but the response depends on uptake and circuit conditions.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Chapter 19 (Closed-Circuit Anesthesia); specific passage/page verification pending

questions.stem: Which group contains only processed electroencephalogram (EEG) measures used as adjuncts to anesthetic depth assessment?
options: Bispectral index (BIS), patient state index, and entropy
questions.explanation: Bispectral index, patient state index, and entropy are processed EEG-derived measures used as adjuncts to clinical assessment. They are not substitutes for evaluating the patient and end-tidal anesthetic concentrations.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 19, printed p. 435 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: After a rapid increase in end-tidal sevoflurane concentration, why may anesthetic effect at the brain still lag behind the monitor reading?
options: End-tidal concentration never approximates alveolar concentration
Brain anesthetic tension may lag end-tidal tension by several minutes
The vaporizer setting directly measures brain concentration
questions.explanation: End-tidal anesthetic tension is an estimate of alveolar tension, not an instantaneous measure of brain tension. After a rapid change, brain equilibration may lag by approximately 3–5 minutes.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 19, printed p. 436 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: On this circle system, which numbered component is the inspiratory unidirectional valve?
questions.explanation: The inspiratory unidirectional valve permits flow toward the patient and limits reverse flow. Its numbered label must be confirmed using the attached diagram.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Chapter 4 (Breathing Circuits); specific passage/page verification pending

questions.stem: Which numbered component prevents exhaled gas from flowing backward toward the patient?
questions.explanation: The expiratory valve allows gas to leave the patient toward the expiratory limb while preventing reverse flow. Check the diagram to verify its numbered component.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Chapter 4 (Breathing Circuits); specific passage/page verification pending

questions.stem: Which numbered point shows the preferred fresh gas inflow site?
questions.explanation: Fresh-gas inflow is typically positioned downstream of the absorber and upstream of the inspiratory valve. Confirm the numerical label against the provided figure.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Chapter 4 (Breathing Circuits); specific passage/page verification pending

questions.stem: Which numbered component should be tightened to add PEEP during spontaneous ventilation?
questions.explanation: The adjustable pressure-limiting valve vents excess circuit gas during manual or spontaneous ventilation. Adjusting it can alter circuit pressure, but it is not a substitute for controlled PEEP.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Chapter 4 (Breathing Circuits); specific passage/page verification pending

questions.stem: In this circle, apparatus dead space begins at which numbered point?
questions.explanation: Apparatus dead space generally begins distal to the inspiratory–expiratory limb junction, including the Y-piece and patient-side connections. Confirm the numbered point in the figure.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Chapter 4 (Breathing Circuits); specific passage/page verification pending

questions.stem: Which numbered component lets the provider assess ventilation visually and squeeze breaths by hand?
questions.explanation: The reservoir bag provides a visual indication of gas movement and can be compressed to manually ventilate the patient. Confirm its numbered label in the image.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Chapter 4 (Breathing Circuits); specific passage/page verification pending

questions.stem: Inspired CO2 rises, and both valves pass the machine check. Which numbered component should be checked next?
questions.explanation: Exhausted CO₂ absorbent permits rebreathing and raises inspired CO₂ despite functioning valves. Identify the absorber in the labeled diagram before selecting a component number.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Chapter 4 (Breathing Circuits); specific passage/page verification pending

questions.stem: If numbered component 2 fails open, which part of the circuit becomes apparatus dead space?
options: The inspiratory limb from the valve onward
The expiratory limb from the Y to the valve
questions.explanation: An incompetent expiratory valve permits reverse flow and rebreathing of expired gas from the expiratory limb, effectively increasing circuit dead space.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Chapter 4 (Breathing Circuits); specific passage/page verification pending

questions.stem: Which desirable feature of a breathing circuit allows rapid adjustment of the patient's anesthetic exposure?
questions.explanation: Rapid changes in delivered gas composition allow the clinician to alter inspired anesthetic concentration when needed. The circuit should also provide low resistance, humidification, and waste-gas removal.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed p. 100 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Which desirable breathing-circuit function is supported by a waste-gas scavenger connection?
questions.explanation: The scavenger collects excess anesthetic gases exiting the circuit and reduces contamination of the operating-room environment. Carbon dioxide removal within a circle circuit is performed separately by the absorbent.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed p. 100 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Why does a low-flow circle system generally conserve inspired heat and humidity better than a high-flow Mapleson circuit?
options: The absorber cools the rebreathed gas
High flows add water vapor to the gas
More warm, humid exhaled gas is rebreathed
questions.explanation: A low-flow circle system rebreathes a larger proportion of the patient's warmed, humidified exhaled gas after carbon dioxide absorption. High fresh-gas flow replaces more of that gas with relatively dry supplied gas.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 19, printed p. 433 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Why can reducing fresh-gas flow in a rebreathing circle system help preserve inspired humidity?
options: Rebreathed gas returns warm and moist
Low flow reduces the patient’s water loss to zero
Fresh gas is fully humidified by the machine
The absorber dries gas passing through it
questions.explanation: Lower fresh-gas flow allows a larger fraction of warm, humid exhaled gas to be rebreathed. This reduces the amount of relatively dry fresh gas replacing the conditioned gas.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 19, printed p. 433 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: What is the function of the adjustable pressure-limiting (pop-off) valve in a Mapleson circuit?
options: Vents gas but doesn't prevent rebreathing
questions.explanation: The pop-off valve releases excess circuit gas, but its presence does not itself prevent rebreathing. In Mapleson systems, CO₂ elimination also depends on fresh-gas flow, circuit arrangement, and breathing pattern.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed p. 114 (complete revised answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Which feature distinguishes a circle breathing system from a conventional Mapleson system?
options: Similar parts, but only the circle has an absorber
Mapleson has separate limbs; the circle has one tube
Both have absorbers, but only the circle has a bag
Neither one uses a dedicated fresh gas inlet
questions.explanation: Circle systems contain a CO₂ absorber and separate unidirectional inspiratory and expiratory flow paths. Conventional Mapleson systems lack an absorber and depend on fresh-gas dilution and venting for CO₂ elimination.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed p. 115 (complete revised answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Why does corrugated breathing-circuit tubing promote turbulent gas flow?
questions.explanation: Corrugations disrupt the flow profile and promote radial and longitudinal mixing. The textbook specifically identifies tubing corrugations as a reason circuit flow is often turbulent.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed p. 103 (complete revised answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: During manual ventilation, the adjustable pressure-limiting valve is accidentally closed while fresh gas continues to enter. Which reservoir-bag property affects the pressure that may develop?
options: The bag absorbs CO2 at higher pressures
Bag pressure never reaches the patient
The bag deflates as circuit pressure rises
The bag's material and pressure-volume characteristics
questions.explanation: An overinflated reservoir bag has a nonlinear pressure-volume relationship, and the pressure achieved depends on its material and construction. A closed relief valve can permit hazardous pressure buildup; the bag must not be assumed to protect the patient.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed p. 106 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: By which airway location has most normal inspired-gas heating and humidification occurred?
questions.explanation: The nasal passages and upper airway warm and humidify inspired gas as it travels distally. The textbook states that most conditioning has occurred by the mid-trachea.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed p. 184 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: In a child ventilated for a prolonged period with dry gas and no heat-and-moisture exchanger, which effect may occur?
options: Worsened hypothermia from airway heat loss
Hyperthermia from friction in the airways
questions.explanation: Prolonged delivery of dry inspired gas increases respiratory heat and moisture loss. Inadequate humidification can worsen hypothermia, particularly in neonates and children.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed p. 185 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: During closed-circuit or low-flow anesthesia, what supplies most of the patient's inspired gas mixture?
options: Room air entrained at the Y
questions.explanation: At low fresh-gas flows, the majority of inspired gas is rebreathed exhaled gas after CO₂ removal. Fresh gas supplements that recycled volume to replace uptake and maintain target inspired gas tensions.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 19, printed p. 433 (complete revised answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: How should fresh gas be supplied during low-flow anesthesia to maintain the desired inspired gas mixture?
options: As pure O2 only, with agent from rebreathing
In the quantity and mix that reach target tensions
At twice the patient’s minute ventilation
Only during inspiration, timed to the breath
questions.explanation: Fresh gas must be supplied in the quantity and composition needed to replace uptake and maintain desired inspired gas tensions. Neither a fixed multiple of minute ventilation nor oxygen-only inflow is universally appropriate.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 19, printed p. 433 (complete revised answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: During ongoing volatile anesthetic uptake at low fresh-gas flow, why might a semiclosed circle require a vaporizer setting higher than the desired inspired anesthetic concentration?
options: Higher settings prevent awareness from brain lag
The vaporizer underdelivers at every flow
The absorber destroys agent passing through
Low-tension exhaled gas dilutes the fresh gas
questions.explanation: At low fresh-gas flow, more exhaled gas mixes with the fresh-gas stream. During ongoing uptake, exhaled anesthetic tension is usually lower than inspired tension, so a higher delivered concentration may be needed to maintain the inspired target.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 19, printed p. 436 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Why is a reservoir bag needed for a spontaneously breathing patient when fresh-gas flow is below peak inspiratory flow?
options: Fresh gas is too humid to inhale
questions.explanation: Peak inspiratory flow can greatly exceed the continuous fresh-gas flow supplied by the anesthesia machine. The reservoir bag stores gas between breaths so that sufficient flow is available during inspiration.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed p. 105 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Which circuit design uses a fresh-gas tube inside an outer expiratory tube?
options: It absorbs CO2 from the outer tube
It converts the circuit to a Mapleson A
It makes the circuit a closed system
It is a coaxial Mapleson D
questions.explanation: The Bain circuit is a coaxial Mapleson D arrangement, with fresh gas delivered through an inner tube toward the patient. Exhaled gas returns through the surrounding outer tube toward the bag-end pop-off valve.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed p. 117 (complete revised answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: A circle circuit has a CO₂ absorber, permits partial rebreathing, and vents excess gas through its open APL valve. How is it classified?
questions.explanation: A semiclosed system allows partial rebreathing while excess gas is vented from the circuit. A fully closed system instead retains the non-CO₂ exhaled gas and replaces only uptake and losses.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed p. 101 (complete revised answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Membrane-based hydrophobic HMEs lose efficiency with which change?
questions.explanation: An HME conserves exhaled heat and water for the next inspiration. Efficiency can vary with tidal volume, minute ventilation, and device construction, so the specific membrane-related claim requires device data.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment, 3e, Ch. 7, Humidification and Filtration (chapter-associated; exact question-specific printed page and full answer set not verified)

questions.stem: In the bacterial or viral filtration efficiency (BFE/VFE) test described in Ehrenwerth, what is the approximate challenge-aerosol droplet diameter?
questions.explanation: The described BFE/VFE test uses nonpathogenic challenge aerosols in droplets approximately 3.0 µm in diameter. This differs from the 0.3-µm most-penetrating-particle-size salt test.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed pp. 186 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: When assessing inhaled anesthetic depth, end-tidal agent tension most directly approximates which sequential compartments?
questions.explanation: End-tidal agent tension approximates alveolar tension, which in turn approximates arterial anesthetic tension under appropriate physiologic conditions. Brain tension may lag after rapid changes, so end-tidal concentration is not an instantaneous effect-site measurement.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 19, printed pp. 434–436 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Which statement is correct about oxygen balance in a nonclosed low-flow breathing circuit?
options: O2 delivery above uptake may still let FiO2 fall
FiO2 rises when the APL is open
O2 delivery above uptake always raises FiO2
FiO2 can't fall if the absorber works
questions.explanation: Oxygen leaves a nonclosed circuit in the gas vented to the scavenging system. Consequently, inspired oxygen can fall despite oxygen inflow exceeding metabolic uptake, so inspired oxygen concentration must be monitored.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 19, printed pp. 448–449 (complete revised question and answer set independently verified)

questions.stem: Which respiratory complication can follow inadequate humidification during mechanical ventilation?
options: It improves V/Q by drying the alveoli
It has no effect on V/Q matching
It eliminates shunt in dependent lung
Thick secretions, atelectasis, and ventilation-perfusion mismatch
questions.explanation: Insufficient humidity increases secretion viscosity and impairs mucociliary clearance. Retained secretions can obstruct airways and contribute to atelectasis and ventilation-perfusion mismatch.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed p. 185 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Why does endotracheal intubation shift the work of warming and humidifying inspired gas toward the lower airway?
options: The ETT adds water directly to the trachea
The ETT bypasses the conditioning airway
questions.explanation: An endotracheal tube bypasses much of the upper airway, reducing normal heat and moisture exchange. The isothermic saturation boundary therefore shifts distally unless inspired gas is appropriately conditioned.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed pp 183–184 (complete revised answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: During stable closed-circuit anesthesia, fresh-gas inflow is adjusted to match what?
options: Uptake of each administered gas or vapor, including oxygen
questions.explanation: In a truly closed circuit, fresh-gas input balances uptake of each administered gas or vapor. When this balance is achieved, total circuit volume and individual gas concentrations can remain constant.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 19, printed pp. 440–441 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Which Mapleson A feature helps minimize carbon dioxide rebreathing during spontaneous ventilation?
options: Fresh gas at the patient end with the valve at the bag
No pop-off, with venting through an open bag tail
An absorber placed right at the patient end
A patient-end pop-off valve that vents near end-exhalation
questions.explanation: The Mapleson A configuration positions the relief valve near the patient, favoring venting of carbon dioxide-rich gas at the end of spontaneous expiration. Its efficiency still depends on adequate fresh-gas flow and breathing pattern.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp. 114–115 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Which Mapleson D arrangement favors carbon dioxide elimination during controlled ventilation?
options: A bag-end pop-off valve that vents during inspiration
No fresh gas inlet anywhere in the circuit
Two one-way valves separating the limbs
Pop-off at the patient end venting at end-exhalation
questions.explanation: Mapleson D positions the pop-off valve near the reservoir bag, with fresh gas entering near the patient. During assisted or controlled ventilation, this arrangement can preferentially vent expired gas when the bag is squeezed.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed p. 115 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Why must a breathing circuit minimize the rebreathing of carbon dioxide from previously exhaled gas?
options: To keep inspired CO2 near zero
questions.explanation: Excess inspired CO₂ can produce hypercapnia and respiratory acidosis. Circle systems can safely rebreathe other exhaled gases because chemical absorbent removes their CO₂ before reinspiration.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp 100–101 (complete revised answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Which effect of excessive airway humidification is described in the textbook?
questions.explanation: Excessive humidification can cause airway condensation and impair mucociliary transport. The textbook identifies surfactant dilution, atelectasis, and ventilation-perfusion mismatch among possible consequences.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed p. 185 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: In the circle breathing systems described in the textbook, the fresh-gas inlet is commonly incorporated with which component?
options: The expiratory valve housing on the limb
The inspiratory unidirectional valve or carbon dioxide absorber housing
questions.explanation: The textbook describes fresh-gas inlet connections at the inspiratory valve or carbon dioxide absorber housing. The preferred inflow site is between the absorber and inspiratory valve, although equipment designs vary.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed p. 106 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: How do circle and to-and-fro breathing systems remove CO₂ from rebreathed gas?
options: Dilution with high fresh gas flow
questions.explanation: Circle and to-and-fro systems rely on chemical absorption of exhaled CO₂. This differs from Mapleson arrangements, which remove CO₂ through fresh-gas dilution and venting.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed p. 101 (complete revised answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Which system removes CO₂ by the same mechanism as a to-and-fro breathing circuit?
questions.explanation: Both to-and-fro and circle systems remove exhaled CO₂ by chemical absorption before rebreathing. Their circuit layouts differ, but neither depends solely on high fresh-gas flow to eliminate CO₂.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed p. 101 (complete revised answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Under normal physiology, how does the upper airway recover heat and moisture during exhalation?
options: A heat sink that loses everything
By acting as a countercurrent heat-and-moisture exchanger
questions.explanation: The upper airway warms and humidifies inspired gas, then recovers part of that heat and moisture as exhaled gas cools and condenses on the mucosa. The textbook describes this as a countercurrent heat-and-moisture exchange function.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 7, printed p. 184 (complete answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: In which circuit is inspired volatile-anesthetic concentration most influenced by the concentration in rebreathed exhaled gas?
options: Semi-closed circle at very high FGF
questions.explanation: At low fresh-gas flow, a semiclosed circle rebreathed fraction rises, increasing the influence of exhaled agent concentration on inspired concentration. Higher fresh-gas flow reduces that dependence.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 19, printed p. 436 (complete revised answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: In a circle breathing system, which three malfunctions can cause inspired carbon dioxide to rise? Select three.
options: A correctly sized reservoir bag with no leak
A properly sealed absorber with fresh absorbent
Appropriate fresh-gas flow through a functioning circle system
questions.explanation: Exhausted absorbent permits carbon dioxide to pass through the circle without removal. Incompetent inspiratory or expiratory unidirectional valves can also allow rebreathing, producing inspired CO₂ on the capnogram.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 23, printed pp. 496–497; Ch. 10, printed p. 242

questions.stem: Which two breathing systems remove exhaled CO₂ through chemical absorption? Select two.
questions.explanation: Circle and to-and-fro systems use chemical absorbent to remove CO₂ from rebreathed gas. Open-drop and Mapleson systems instead eliminate CO₂ by venting and/or dilution with fresh gas.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed p. 101 (complete revised answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Which three statements about conventional Mapleson breathing systems are correct? Select three.
options: One tube serves inspiration and expiration
CO2 removal depends on FGF and breathing pattern
They need less fresh gas than a circle
Mapleson A is best for controlled ventilation
questions.explanation: Conventional Mapleson systems lack CO₂ absorbent and separate inspiratory and expiratory one-way limbs. Their CO₂ elimination depends on fresh-gas flow, circuit configuration, and the patient's respiratory pattern; a pop-off valve alone cannot prevent rebreathing.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed pp 114–115 (complete revised answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Which result from prolonged underhumidification? Select 3.
options: Falsely high volumes from wet flow sensors
Thick secretions that obstruct the ETT
Distal shift of the isothermic saturation boundary
questions.explanation: Inadequate humidification dries airway mucus, impairs mucociliary clearance, and can cause secretion plugging. The isothermic saturation boundary shifts distally when the conditioning upper airway is bypassed; reduced compliance may follow airway obstruction or atelectasis.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment, 3e, Ch. 7, Humidification and Filtration (chapter-associated; exact question-specific printed page and full answer set not verified)

questions.stem: Which three features are advantages of closed-circuit anesthesia? Select three.
options: Rebreathed gas is already warm and humid
questions.explanation: Closed-circuit anesthesia reduces anesthetic waste, environmental pollution, and agent costs. Rebreathed exhaled gas is already warm and humidified, although CO₂ absorption and appropriate gas monitoring remain necessary.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 19, printed p. 433 (complete revised answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Which two statements describe the adjustable pressure-limiting (APL) valve? Select two.
options: Directs inspiratory gas toward the patient
Lets excess gas leave the circuit to the scavenger
Can create PEEP during spontaneous ventilation when tightened
Sits between the absorber and inspiratory valve
questions.explanation: The APL valve releases excess gas from the manual breathing circuit toward scavenging. Tightening the valve increases the pressure required for venting and can generate positive end-expiratory pressure during spontaneous breathing.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed p. 106 (complete revised answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Which two listed airway regions contribute substantially to humidification of inspired gases? Select two.
questions.explanation: The mucous membranes of the nose, trachea, and bronchi contain many mucus glands and perform much of airway humidification. The nasopharynx, pharynx, and larynx contribute relatively little; among the listed options, the nose and trachea are the two best answers.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Chapter 7, printed p. 185

questions.stem: Fresh-gas flow is reduced from 8 to 1 L/min in a semiclosed circle system. Which effects are expected? Select two.
options: Inspired anesthetic concentration always rises at the same dial setting
Inspired concentration becomes independent of exhaled anesthetic
The vaporizer must always be turned down
Changes in inspired anesthetic concentration occur more slowly
questions.explanation: Reducing fresh-gas flow increases the fraction of exhaled gas rebreathed in a circle system. Lower flow also slows changes in inspired anesthetic concentration, so the vaporizer may need adjustment but does not invariably have to be turned up or down.
questions.citation: Elisha, Heiner, & Nagelhout (2023), Nurse Anesthesia, 7th ed., Chapter 16, printed pp. 266–267

questions.stem: Which two functions explain why a breathing circuit uses a reservoir bag? Select two.
options: Machine FGF can't meet peak inspiratory flow
It removes CO2 from exhaled gas
It filters bacteria from the circuit
questions.explanation: The reservoir bag stores gas for inspiration when instantaneous inspiratory demand exceeds machine fresh-gas delivery. It also allows manual ventilation and provides a visual indication of breathing.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 4, printed p. 105 (complete revised answer verified against inspected passage)

questions.stem: Which signs are integrated when assessing anesthetic depth? Select 3.
questions.explanation: Anesthetic depth is assessed using multiple findings, including processed EEG when appropriate, hemodynamic responses, and clinical signs such as pupillary changes. No single one of these measures reliably determines consciousness in every patient.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment, 3e, Ch. 4, Breathing Circuits (chapter-associated; exact question-specific printed page and full answer set not verified)

questions.stem: Which three statements accurately compare mainstream and sidestream capnography? Select three.
options: Sidestream sampling adds transport delay before the gas reaches the analyzer
Mainstream requires a sampling tube to a remote analyzer
Sidestream uses sampling tubing between the airway and analyzer
Mainstream sensors are immune to secretions and moisture
Sidestream sampling has no response delay
Mainstream has no sampling-line transport delay
questions.explanation: Sidestream capnography transports gas through sampling tubing, introducing transit delay before analysis. Mainstream sensing occurs at the airway, avoiding sampling-line transport delay, although sensor contamination and other response limitations remain possible.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 10, printed p. 242 (Table 10.2)

questions.stem: Which two technologies are commonly used to measure inspired oxygen concentration in anesthesia breathing systems? Select two.
options: Mass spectrometry as the only contemporary option
questions.explanation: Contemporary inspired-oxygen analyzers commonly use paramagnetic sensors or galvanic fuel cells. A flowmeter measures gas flow rather than directly measuring inspired oxygen concentration, while colorimetric detectors measure carbon dioxide.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Ch. 8, printed p. 207

questions.stem: Which capnography findings suggest a problem with the patient's airway or breathing rather than equipment? Select 3.
options: Baseline that doesn't return to zero
No waveform after a circuit disconnect
Gradual EtCO2 rise with stable settings
Sudden loss of waveform with zero airway pressure
